message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description | Notes |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average) | Weighted average of isotopes H‑1, H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium). |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among all elements. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | Energy to remove the single valence electron. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) | Small negative value; hydrogen does not readily accept an extra electron. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; hydrogen is a gas at room temperature. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Solidifies only at cryogenic temperatures. |
| **Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.08988 g cm⁻³ | About 14.7 times lighter than air. |
| **Molar volume (ideal gas, 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | Standard molar volume. |
| **Molecular weight of H₂** | 2.016 g mol⁻¹ | Two hydrogen atoms per molecule. |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ | Energy required to break H₂ into two H atoms. |
| **Dipole moment** | 0 D (non‑polar) | Homonuclear diatomic molecule. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series | Characteristic hydrogen emission/absorption lines. |
| **Isotopes** | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) | Deuterium is stable; tritium is radioactive (half‑life ~12.3 y). |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (H₂) | Hydrogen can act as an acid (H⁺) or base (H⁻). |
| **Acidity/basicity** | pKa of H₃O⁺ ≈ –1.7 (strong acid); pKb of H₂O ≈ 15.7 (weak base) | Hydrogen behaves as a proton donor in aqueous solutions. |
| **Reactivity** | Combines with most non‑metals; reacts with oxygen to form H₂O; with halogens to form HX; with metals to form hydrides. | Highly reactive due to high electronegativity and small size. |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive mixture with air (4–75 % H₂). | Requires ignition source; flame temperature ~2800 °C. |
| **Solubility in water** | 1.6 g L⁻¹ at 20 °C | Low solubility; hydrogen gas escapes quickly. |
| **Electrical conductivity** | Very low in gaseous state; increases dramatically when ionized (plasma). | Ionized hydrogen (protons) can conduct electricity in electrolytes. |
| **Magnetic properties** | Diamagnetic (no unpaired electrons). | Weakly repelled by magnetic fields. |
| **Phase diagram** | Triple point at 13.99 K, 0.0002 MPa; critical point at 33.41 K, 1.3 MPa. | Hydrogen remains a gas above 33 K under normal pressure. |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), rocket propellant, industrial hydrogenation, laboratory reagent, plasma generation. | Key role in clean energy research. |

---

### Quick Summary

- **Atomic & Molecular**: Hydrogen is the lightest element, with a single proton and one valence electron. Its diatomic form (H₂) is a colorless, odorless gas.
- **Physical**: Extremely low boiling/melting points, very low density, high ionization energy, and high electronegativity.
- **Chemical**: Acts as both an acid (H⁺) and a base (H⁻), forms hydrides with metals, reacts explosively with oxygen, and is highly flammable.
- **Isotopic Variants**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable, heavier), tritium (radioactive).
- **Industrial & Energy**: Central to fuel cells, rocket propulsion, and many chemical synthesis processes.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
